text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
- Between a quarter and a third of Hungary's population lives below the poverty line, according to the latest Central Statistical Office figures.

- President of the opposition Smallholders Party Joszef Torgyan expressed his backing for deputy parlaimentary speaker Agnes Nagyne Maczo, who has been asked to step down. Torgyan said attempts to remove Maczo can be regarded as a fascist initiative.
- Twenty rail wagons full of petrol have disappeared from Kiskoros railway station.

- President of the Roma parliament Jeno Zsigo said Hungary's law on minorities is biased against the Roma population and added that the situation of gypsies has deteriorated since Communism ended seven years ago.
